defect.description: Isinstance(self.log_output, TextIO) never matches a real file: typing.TextIO is not a base class of what open() returns (io.TextIOWrapper, or the io.BufferedWriter of the default os.devnull log), so stop() still leaves every file log open, as before; it should test io.IOBase (or for a close method).

review_items: Default log_output=None opens devnull in binary mode; isinstance(TextIO) false for BufferedWriter so it is never closed
Removed try/except around close lets a failed close skip process termination
isinstance(obj, TextIO) relies on Python 3.12+ typing internals; use io.TextIOBase
isinstance dispatch misses BinaryIO/custom file-likes; use hasattr close or io.IOBase
No test covers text-file or default-path closing
votes.evidence_quote: stop() checks isinstance(TextIO) which is False for BinaryIO (BufferedWriter), and it is not an int either. The file handle is never closed, leaking a file descriptor every time a Service with default log_output is stopped.
votes.justification: The review pins the leak on the isinstance(TextIO) check in stop() and shows the default os.devnull BufferedWriter is never closed. It also recommends an io.IOBase check. It wrongly claims text files match on 3.12+, but the core defect, cause and fix at the right code are reported.
